sources.name: PhishDesk synthetic generator
sources.contains: phishing and legitimate (invented brands, reserved domains)
sources.notes: Generated by scripts in this repo; fully reproducible from seeds.

sources.name: Nazario phishing corpus
sources.contains: phishing (hand-classified by the publisher; may contain errors)
sources.attribution: Jose Nazario, Nazario Phishing Corpus, https://monkey.org/~jose/phishing/ (CC-BY-4.0)
sources.notes: Recent years are not anonymized and contain real addresses: raw files are never committed, only labels.

sources.name: Apache SpamAssassin public mail corpus (ham only)
sources.licence: No explicit licence. Readme says messages were posted to public fora or donated.
sources.contains: legitimate (easy_ham, hard_ham); spam folders not used
sources.notes: Old (2002-2003). Some headers obfuscated. Decide: approved-local or do-not-use.

sources.name: Enron email dataset (CMU, May 2015 version)
sources.licence: No explicit licence. Public FERC release, distributed by CMU as a research resource.
sources.attribution: Enron Email Dataset, CALO Project / William W. Cohen, CMU
sources.notes: Real people's mail; CMU asks users to be sensitive to their privacy. Large archive. Decide: approved-local or do-not-use.
